title: Play Action Logbook: RBAC-aware Evidence Export & SIEM Mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical logbook for on-call responders and security engineers to:
- quickly collect and export forensic evidence in an RBAC v2 environment,
- verify audit log schema coverage, and
- map exported artifacts into the SIEM ingestion pipeline.

Scope / audience:
- On-call security engineers and SREs.
- Solutions engineers asked to produce evidence for customers or compliance review.

Quick triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Identify incident vectors: user-conflict vs. system compromise vs. data exfiltration.
2) Confirm RBAC constraints: which roles can perform log export? (see RBAC note).
3) Freeze export window: record timeframe and sampling strategy (full vs. quick sample).
4) Start evidence export job (automated pipeline preferred). If automation unavailable, follow manual export commands below.
5) Create incident ticket and attach export manifest (ticket id in artifact names).

RBAC v2 considerations (practical):
- Principle: least privilege for exporters. "export:logs" and "export:siem_submit" are separate permissions.
- Typical safe roles: security-admin (exp limited) and audit-operator.
- Avoid using high-privilege service accounts for ad-hoc exports — use short-lived delegation (STS) where possible.
- If an oncall is blocked by RBAC, escalate to oncall-priv-escalation (see Escalation matrix). Note the escalation steps are logged and must be recorded in ticket.

Audit log schema checklist (fields we must capture for SIEM mapping):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- service (e.g., api-gateway, console, infra-agent)
- tenant_id / org_id / project_id
- actor_type (user|service|system)
- actor_id (user email, service principal)
- actor_ip (ipv4/ipv6) – if NAT present, include source NAT metadata
- action (string e.g., token.create, model.invoke)
- resource_type (token, model, deployment)
- resource_id (string)
- result (success|failure|denied)
- outcome_detail (http status, error code)
- request_payload_hash (sha256) — optional but useful for evidence linking
- response_sample_digest (short)
- kv_evidence_refs (list of storage handles)
- chain_of_custody_id (coc-xxxx)

Note: retention_policy and tenant-redaction flags should be included for export, otherwise SIEM ingestion may require additional PII handling.

Example minimal audit snippet (pseudo):
- timestamp: 2024-11-05T09:12:22Z
- event_id: e8f2a1b4-6d3a-4b8e-9a2d-11c5b2f7a999
- service: api-gateway
- actor_type: user
- actor_id: maya@redwood.ai
- actor_ip: 34.82.132.11
- action: deployment.update
- resource_type: deployment
- resource_id: dpl-7a3e
- result: denied
- outcome_detail: 403 RBAC_DENY

Automated evidence export pipeline (preferred):
1) Kick off export via internal service 'audit-exporter' (recommended, avoids manual RBAC ops).
   - API: POST /v1/exports with payload { window_start, window_end, filter_query, redaction_level, ticket_id }
   - Exporter will: validate RBAC, stage objects to secure bucket, compute checksums, sign chain_of_custody metadata, and emit export manifest.json to /coc/exports/<ticket_id>.json
2) Watch exporter job in /observability/exports dashboard; if job fails with 4xx permission error, capture error blob and escalate.
3) After export success, run 'siem-ingest' job (or open PR to stream if manual). Include manifest reference and coc id in SIEM event.

Manual export steps (if exporter not functioning):
- For API gateway logs: run privileged query in audit-store (Elastic) -> filter by event.time and service:api-gateway -> dump to secured GCS bucket.
- For console session recordings: retrieve session artifacts from session-store using session_id(s).
- Compute sha256 checksums for every artifact and write checksum manifest.
- Create chain_of_custody metadata file (who pulled, why, destination).
- Encrypt artifacts with customer key (if required) and attach manifest to incident ticket.

SIEM mapping & parsing notes (index time):
- Map 'actor_id' -> siem.user_identity
- Map 'resource_type' & 'action' -> siem.event_action (join for richer rules)
- Map outcome_detail to siem.event_status and siem.error_code
- Add fields: siem.coc_id, siem.export_manifest_url, siem.original_event_id for linkage
- Precompute event hashes to support dedupe across streaming and batch export pipelines.

Detection rules to enable on exported fields (examples):
- High volume of denied RBAC actions from single actor_ip within 5m -> create alert (possible auth brute).
- Cross-tenant access attempts where actor_tenant != resource_tenant -> escalate to sec-privilege-lateral.
- Unusual model checkpoint downloads (resource_type=model and action=artifact.download) -> immediate hold and CSM notification.

Common incident scenarios & play actions:
1) Suspicious service principal activity (no console login)
   - Export service audit logs and related infra telemetry, collect credentials rotation events, rotate keys for implicated principal.
2) Unauthorized console access (user impersonation)
   - Collect session recordings, list of actions, mapping of resources touched, and immediate RBAC role-review for the user and recently altered groups.
3) SIEM ingestion gap discovered (missing events)
   - Check exporter manifest, re-run exporter for the missing window, validate delivery receipts (S3 etags).

Chain of custody (quick template):
- coc_id: coc-<ticket>-<YYYYMMDD>-<random>
- created_by: <oncall name>
- created_at: <iso-ts>
- source_refs: [list storage URIs]
- checksum_manifest: uri
- recipient: security-team@redwood.ai
- retention_until: 2025-01-01 (example)
- notes: brief reason for export

Escalation matrix (summary):
- If RBAC blocks export and business-critical: escalate to Security Lead (Diego) -> SLA 30 min.
- If evidence at risk of tampering: engage SRE for short-term frozen snapshot and legal if PII involved.

Post-incident checklist (what to attach to postmortem):
- export_manifest.json and coc metadata (sha256 verified)
- SIEM ingest receipts + parsing logs
- RBAC change diff (who changed what and when)
- Timeline with actions and actor_ids (minute granularity)
- Notes on missing fields and schema gaps (needed for Improve stage)

Operational TODOs (observations from recent incidents):
- Add request_payload_hash to default audit schema for all APIs (open PR: github/58).
- Improve exporter error messages to include failing RBAC policy id.
- Add automated redaction pipeline to strip sensitive parameters before SIEM ingest.

Appendix A — Quick commands (placeholders, adapt to environment):
- Start exporter: curl -X POST https://internal/audit-exporter/v1/exports -d '{ window_start:"2024-11-05T09:00:00Z", window_end:"2024-11-05T09:15:00Z", filter:"actor_id:maya@redwood.ai", ticket_id:"INC-4321" }' 
- Verify manifest: gsutil cat gs://redwood-sec-exports/coc/INC-4321.json | jq .
- Compute checksum: sha256sum artifact.tar.gz > artifact.sha256

Unresolved questions / notes to follow up:
- Need guidance on export consent for EU tenant data when legal holds are present. (action: Priya)
- Confirm exact retention SLA for security exports vs. standard audit retention. (action: Samir)

Related docs and hooks:
- Confluence -> SEC-EXPORT-PIPELINE (design + diagrams)
- Jira -> SEC-2314 (exporter RBAC hardening)
- GH -> repo/redwood-audit-exporter (current PRs referenced above)

Notes to self (quick):
- if in doubt, create an export and mark it 'redacted' rather than skipping. Export manifests help debugging even when redaction reduces payload utility.
- keep a running mapping table in Confluence for "service -> default_fields" so oncall can decide if extra fields are needed.

End of logbook.

Revision history:
- 2024-10-12: initial draft by Maya Chen
- 2024-11-05: updates for exporter API & RBAC notes (collaborators: Priya, Diego)
